VERIFICATION NOTE - SERBIAN ELECTION DATE. WRITTEN 24 OCT 2026 19:46 BST.

FINDING: Serbia does NOT vote on Saturday 24 October 2026. Serbia votes on SUNDAY
25 OCTOBER 2026. No result, no turnout figure, no exit poll and no preliminary
count exists, because polls have not opened. Nobody is claiming victory and nobody
is disputing a count.

WHAT IS KNOWN AND SAFE TO PUBLISH TONIGHT:
- Snap parliamentary election, Sunday 25 October 2026. Called last month by
  Aleksandar Vucic, who resigned as president in order to run for prime minister.
  He is barred from seeking a third presidential term.
- Vucic's Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) has been in government since 2012. BBC
  frames this as the most serious electoral challenge since then. NPR describes it
  as "14 years of government" by Vucic.
- The challenger is the "Student List", grown out of nearly two years of
  anti-corruption protests triggered by the deaths of 16 people when a railway
  station canopy collapsed at Novi Sad.
- It has no leader and no hierarchy. Student assemblies at university faculties
  selected its 250 candidates. None has a political background.
- Top candidate: Ilija Srdanovic, a cardiologist and professor at Novi Sad
  University. He is NOT the movement's leader and would not necessarily be its
  choice of prime minister.
- Srdanovic to the BBC: "It is absolutely normal to stand with my students to help
  them in their fair struggle." And: "We offer to our citizens the core values of
  civilised society, which this previous regime has taken away from our citizens for
  the last time."
- Vucic has called the movement foreign-backed and said it seeks to "bring down our
  state", telling a final rally: "Let us always protect and defend it."
- Vucic on the Student List and Russia: "When you ask them: will you impose
  sanctions on Russia? Silence, umming and ah-ing, but no answer. You know what the
  Chinese think, you've heard what Vladimir Putin said. So you decide. Think about
  who has our best interests at heart."
- Final rallies, Thursday night: SNS held an arena event in Belgrade with Vucic the
  only speaker. The Student List drew a reported 150,000 to Slavija Square.
- BBC: "Reliable polls are thin on the ground, but analysts are predicting an
  extremely tight vote."
- Magda Anastasijevic, Eastern Europe analyst for the conflict monitor ACLED, to the
  BBC on the Novi Sad canopy collapse: "Vucic has survived this in the past, he was
  always able to find a scapegoat and blame whatever problems on them. This was not
  the case for the canopy."
- At the 2023 parliamentary election the International Election Observation Mission
  noted "overwhelming ruling party advantage" due to "bias in the media" and
  "misuse of public office and resources".
- The BBC approached leading SNS figures for interview and was not offered a response.

CAUTION FOR THE DESK: no approved source reached tonight states the poll opening or
closing times, and none states when preliminary results are expected. Do not assert
a results time. Do not write "counting under way" - counting cannot be under way on
a vote that has not happened.
